values.note: $25 a night on the DNR amenity table (the campground page carries the statewide '$20 for most sites' boilerplate). A Recreation Passport is required for vehicle entry to every state forest campground.

fees.source: https://www.michigan.gov/dnr/things-to-do/camping-and-lodging/state-forest-campgrounds/amenity-table (Houghton Lake State Forest Campground, Roscommon, semi-modern: 50 sites, $25) + https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/houghtonlake ('A Recreation Passport (park pass) is required for vehicle entry into all state park and forest campgrounds'), read 2026-10-25

values.note: Modern restroom building without showers. Drinking water from a hand-pump well. The boating access site for Houghton Lake is off site.

facilities.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/houghtonlake ('Amenities include a modern restroom building (no showers)'; 'There are modern restrooms, but no showers.'; 'There are vault toilets.'; 'Potable (drinking) water is available from a hand-pump well.'; 'The boating access site for Houghton Lake is located off site.'), read 2026-10-25

values.note: No reservations or advance payment. Register by the phone number or website posted at the campground, no earlier than 8 a.m. on the day of arrival; the site must then be set up and occupied. Card, check or cash.

booking.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/houghtonlake ('No reservations. Sites available on a first-come, first-served basis. All registrations now processed online or via phone.'; 'You can register no earlier than 8 a.m. on the day of your arrival. Once you have registered, your campsite must be set up and occupied ... we do not accept advance payments or reservations. Mastercard, Visa, Discover, check and cash accepted.'; 'Camping is limited to a 15-day maximum stay.') + amenity table ('Reservable at MiDNRReservations.com' no), read 2026-10-25

values.note: Sites 'suitable for tent and small trailer use' (the DNR's standard state forest wording). One camping unit and six people per site.

sites.source: https://www.michigan.gov/dnr/things-to-do/camping-and-lodging/state-forest-campgrounds/amenity-table (Houghton Lake State Forest Campground: 50 campsites) + https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/houghtonlake ('The sites are suitable for tent and small trailer use.'; 'One camping unit and six people are allowed per site'), read 2026-10-25

values.note: Closed November to April (DNR amenity table).

season.source: https://www.michigan.gov/dnr/things-to-do/camping-and-lodging/state-forest-campgrounds/amenity-table (Houghton Lake State Forest Campground: 'Seasonal closure dates: November to April'), read 2026-10-25

note: Semi-modern state forest campground on the north shore of Houghton Lake (Michigan's largest inland lake, 20,000+ acres; walleye, pike, bass, perch), 8 mi N of the town of Houghton Lake via West Houghton Lake Drive and Old US 27, Roscommon County; managed by North Higgins Lake State Park. Muskegon River 2 mi west, Higgins Lake 6 mi north. --Claude
summary: DNR page + SF amenity table: 50 sites (confirmed), $25 (table; confirmed) + Recreation Passport, no electric, modern restrooms without showers + vault toilets, hand-pump water, first-come only with same-day online/phone registration from 8 a.m., 15-day maximum (inherited max now confirmed), closed November to April (season note added). max_rig_ft 40 (derived from the note) left: the page says only 'tent and small trailer'. Note trimmed of field restatements and its stale '~$20, self-register at kiosk' and 'late April to mid-September'.
flags: Missing phone: the DNR page gives 989-821-6125 (North Higgins Lake SP, as on the amenity table).
